label: Stop Prolonged Beyond Its Original Purpose
motion_heading: The Stop Was Unlawfully Prolonged Beyond Its Original Purpose

review_conditions.display_note: You said police did something else during the stop. Before filing, check that it wasn't part of handling the reason for the stop (e.g. writing the ticket or checking the driver's license); if it was, it doesn't support this argument.
Check that the officer noticed the reasons you listed before beginning the extra investigation. A reason that came up only afterward doesn't justify it.
Police found an outstanding warrant for your client. Expect the prosecution to argue under *Utah v. Strieff* that the warrant attenuates the connection between the stop and the evidence.
If police called for a K-9 unit before the stop's original tasks were done, that timing itself can be favorable: it suggests they meant to prolong the stop regardless of what happened later.

sentences.text: A traffic stop becomes unlawful if it is prolonged beyond the time reasonably required to complete the mission of the stop.
Similarly, the investigative methods employed should be the least intrusive means reasonably available to verify or dispel the officer's suspicion in a short amount of time.

Authority for the seizure ends when tasks tied to the traffic infraction are, or reasonably should have been, completed, and an officer may not extend the stop, even briefly, for unrelated investigation unless the officer has independent reasonable suspicion.
The government bears the burden of establishing that the officer had that suspicion before beginning the additional investigation.
Suspicion that arises only after the officer has begun the additional investigation cannot justify the extension.

“We [] conclude that the request for a passenger's identification is a significant event under the Alaska Constitution — and that an officer is precluded from requesting a passenger's identification and then using that identification to run a warrants check when the officer's request is unrelated to the basis for the stop and the officer has no other case-specific justification for doing so. A routine identification and warrants check on a passenger, without any basis for doing so, runs the risk of ‘turning a routine traffic stop into a “fishing expedition for criminal activity unrelated to the stop” ’ — and thus systematically infringing on Alaskans’ right to privacy.”
A dog sniff is permissible only if it does not add time to the stop.

practice_notes: *Rodriguez* rejects a bright-line minimum delay — even a short, unjustified extension can violate the Fourth Amendment, so don't discount this issue just because the added time was brief.
Get the CAD and any bodycam/dashcam timestamps in discovery early — this issue depends on minute-by-minute sequencing.
_author_notes: Timing redesign 2026-10-08 (the maintainer): Rodriguez forbids adding time with unrelated inquiries whenever they happen, not only after the stop's tasks are done. q_original_purpose_completed was removed, and q_extension_event and q_independent_suspicion were reworded to drop the before/after framing (q_independent_suspicion was later replaced by q_extension_reasons).

passenger_identification: text and citation supplied by the maintainer (2026-10-08). Perozzo is a prolongation case: an unnecessary passenger ID and warrants check is one way of unlawfully prolonging the stop. Alaska only (no federal authority yet). Two open items: the quote needs its quoting parenthetical for the 'fishing expedition' language (the maintainer will supply it); and 'We [] conclude' is kept exactly as given, but the empty brackets look like a lost omission marker. Inner quotation marks were alternated (double outside, then single, then double) because the passage is now itself a quotation.
Perozzo's 'no other case-specific justification': since 2026-10-12 nothing in the match requires a lack of justification. q_extension_reasons collects the officer's stated reasons.

least_intrusive_means: text and citation (Royer at 500) supplied by the maintainer, 2026-10-08. Verify: as I recall, the part of Royer containing this passage was a plurality opinion (four Justices). Not checked against the opinion.

'Something else (e.g. investigating a different crime)' gets the other_extension_activity review note (Claude draft). The note's examples of mission tasks (ticket, driver's license) are from Rodriguez as I recall it; check before relying on it.

2026-10-12 (the maintainer chose option A, to revisit during legal review): q_independent_suspicion ('did the officer have independent reasonable suspicion?') asked for a legal conclusion and was replaced by q_extension_reasons, the officer's stated reasons for beginning to investigate another crime. strieff_attenuation review note (2026-10-12): drafted by Claude. Strieff (2016) as I recall it: discovering a valid, pre-existing arrest warrant after an unlawful stop attenuated the connection to evidence found in the search incident to the arrest. From memory, unverified. The maintainer chose to show the note in both courts for now.

TO CHECK (the maintainer, 2026-10-12): does Alaska follow Strieff under the Alaska Constitution, or has it rejected or limited it? The strieff_attenuation note prints in state court until this is checked.

It was a prosecution-friendly permission with the rejected before/after framing, and authority_ends_at_mission_completion already states the rule as a limit ('unless the officer has independent reasonable suspicion').
